_provenance.notes: Pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) is the most abundant Pacific salmon by far — Alaska harvests 150-350 million pinks per year. Pinks have the shortest life cycle of all salmon (strict 2-year life cycle), creating strong even-year/odd-year population cycles in most rivers. Southern Southeast Alaska and Prince William Sound have dominant odd-year populations; Bristol Bay and Kodiak tend to have mixed or even-year dominance. Pink salmon represent over 40% of all salmon harvested in Alaska by number, but have the lowest ex-vessel value ($0.20-0.40/lb). The primary markets are Japanese fish meal, canned salmon, and increasingly frozen filet products. Hatchery contributions in PWS are 25-35% of the commercial harvest.

odd_even_year_cycle.description: The pink salmon odd/even year cycle — a fundamental biological phenomenon
odd_even_year_cycle.notes: Pink salmon have a strict 2-year life cycle. Southern populations (SEAK, PWS, Kodiak) tend to have much larger odd-year runs than even-year. Northern populations (Norton Sound, some rivers) tend to have larger even-year runs. The cycle is deeply embedded in the genetics of these populations. Interestingly, hatchery programs have tended to strengthen the dominant-year cycle.
